scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported polygon extends through 1600 to 1878 in the Western Australian Mid West. These map dates are neither establishment nor extinction, and the geometry is not certified as a historical cultural boundary or modern native title area.

Names and groupings differ across linguistic, historical and legal sources. The card uses documented current Amangu identity and regional relationships, not a blanket equation with Nhanda, Wilunyu, Wajarri or every Yamatji person. Language classifications not independently established here are omitted.

The 2016 excavation paper was read in author-uploaded full text after the museum PDF returned 403. Calibrated BP has the 1950 reference point; the card retains that notation rather than silently converting it into a modern relative date. The paper’s approximate 25,500 cal BP is not confused with uncalibrated radiocarbon years or Wikipedia’s different figure.

Table 1 and narrative differ in the stated depth for the oldest charcoal. The card omits a precise depth. The oldest sample came from sieve residue, and a separate deep young fragment was interpreted as intrusive. Neither is described as an undisturbed hearth dated directly in situ.

Stone-tool debris and later hearth-associated ochre are distinct observations. Preliminary faunal analysis attributes deposition to humans, owls and carnivores. No universal diet, village size, uninterrupted occupation or ancient political identity is inferred.

The university news report and excavation article concern the same project. Their combined derived runtime prose and source notes must stay within a conservative 200-word budget. The paper acknowledges Thomas Cameron, Buddy Edwards and Reg Brockman; the public card does not invent their individual excavation roles.

Regional trail examples identify shared fishing and water resources. Public sites and community knowledge are discussed without assigning every local site exclusively to Amangu people or reproducing restricted cultural details. General claims of 40,000-year occupation in the stock-route assessment are not adopted as site-specific dates.

The 2017 YMAC report is a dated account of claim changes and agreement administration. The 2020 annual report distinguishes the 7 February court event from 24 February formal execution, avoiding the simpler signing date in a February news release. No claim is made that native title was recognized across the entire agreement area or that every benefit has been delivered.

Dickerson’s artwork and the ATOM film guide were downloaded and the relevant pages read. A 2024 to 2025 report date is not taken as a painting creation date. Richardson’s 2021 age, aspirations and student status are not presented as current. Other film participants are not relabeled Amangu.
The producer’s Winthu Wangga description and credits were read; the performance video was not viewed. Public artistic statements are paraphrased without asserting access to restricted stories.
Independent historical review, border assessment and depth certification remain pending.
